verdict: RUNG (c0/s0 reproduce F153): 8 cells, worst error 0.00e+00. Identical. ANTI-VACUITY: 0 model(s) lack room to move both ways, so every model below can show either direction. PRIMARY, does ANY text raise TWO OR MORE of the 6 models? YES -- p1 raises ['Falcon3-1B-Base', 'Minerva-3B-base-v1.0']. F153's empty overlap was a SMALL-SAMPLE ARTEFACT. Some texts DO raise structure across different weights, so 'structure-raising prefix' is a partly coherent category after all, text properties may be partly predictive, and the thesis clause that no prefix can be certified in advance must be withdrawn or heavily qualified. SECONDARY, per-model UP rate over a real corpus: Falcon3-1B-Base raw 0.213: 2/12 up (p1,s2); Minerva-3B-base-v1.0 raw 0.328: 3/12 up (p1,s0,s1); pythia-410m-deduped raw 0.427: 0/12 up (-); Qwen1.5-1.8B raw 0.510: 1/12 up (p2); SmolLM-1.7B raw 0.562: 0/12 up (-); Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct raw 0.573: 0/12 up (-). TERTIARY (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, declared before the numbers -- 6 model clusters cannot fail this test informatively): up-rate by source c=0/18, p=3/36, s=3/18 (c=CORPUS, p=pile, s=shakespeare). F153 logged 'all up-texts were Shakespeare' as an untestable lead; this is the same lead with a real corpus beside it, and it is still not a test. BOUNDARY: 6 models, 12 texts, ONE length (9 tokens), three English sources. An empty overlap over these texts and models is an existence claim, not a proof that no text ever raises two models.
